componentPlan.focusQuote: The Federal Convention convened in the State House (Independence Hall) in Philadelphia on May 14, 1787
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Traces the convention in page order from convening to new draft to signing for cause and effect

componentPlan.focusQuote: how these representatives should be elected—directly by the people or by the state legislators
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Checks recall of central power, representation, and election debates that required compromise

overview.headline: Secret drafting and compromise behind the new Constitution

keyPoints.point: The Convention decided not to amend the Articles but to draft an entirely new frame of government
keyPoints.quote: rather than amend the existing Articles, the Convention would draft an entirely new frame of government

keyPoints.point: Delegates drafted in secret during the summer and signed the document that established the government of the United States
keyPoints.quote: signed on September 17, 1787, established the government of the United States

keyPoints.point: Chief debate covered how much power to allow the central government and how many representatives each state should have
keyPoints.quote: Among the chief points at issue were how much power to allow the central government

keyPoints.point: The Federal Convention convened in Philadelphia and adjourned daily until a quorum of seven states was obtained
keyPoints.quote: until a quorum of seven states was obtained on May 25

keyTerms.gloss: gathering of delegates that debated in secret during the summer
keyTerms.quote: Drafted in secret by delegates to the Constitutional Convention during the summer of 1787

keyTerms.gloss: earlier system that delegates voted to revise in favor of a new frame
keyTerms.quote: to revise the Articles of Confederation

keyTerms.gloss: minimum number of states needed before business could proceed
keyTerms.quote: until a quorum of seven states was obtained on May 25

keyTerms.gloss: national authority whose power was debated by delegates
keyTerms.quote: how much power to allow the central government

analysis.pageCoverage: Introductory overview of the drafting of the Constitution in Philadelphia, from the call to revise the Articles to secret debate, compromise, and signing.
analysis.subject: history
